concerns_addressed: Historical T3 cycle 3 REVIEW_BLOCKED context is preserved: the earlier audit found nested requests entering before transactional critical sections; recovery verified independent HTTP workers/servers and barriers at the order and approval boundaries.

order-flow.test.js now uses real fetch requests against a separately spawned PHP built-in server running Laravel's HTTP kernel, with an isolated SQLite database migrated and seeded before startup and server/database cleanup afterward; it does not replace or mock fetch.

The real HTTP test performs complete registration with required fields, login, authenticated catalog browse, two submissions using the same Idempotency-Key and body identity, admin login/list/approval, and authenticated outlet tracking with status history.

OrderForm retains one idempotency key per cart signature across retry or duplicate submission and clears it only after a successful response; all product, order, tracking, and admin calls send Bearer JWT headers.
The prior missing real-E2E and per-submit-random-key findings are resolved. The API regression suite passes (36 tests, 187 assertions) and the Next.js production build succeeds.

strengths: The E2E setup validates the actual PHP/Laravel process boundary, isolated persistence, onboarding/authentication, authorization, idempotency, approval, and outlet scoping rather than a response script.
The UI idempotency ref is keyed to the logical cart payload and is reused for retries while the submission remains unsuccessful or in flight.
Existing order creation, reservation, idempotency, approval-concurrency, and status-history tests remain green.
